title: Stray Kids Reportedly Join BTS in Skipping Grammy Submissions
summary:
K-pop group Stray Kids is reportedly joining BTS in skipping the Grammy Awards process. Billboard says the company did not explain the eight-member group's decision. But it seems likely that it is a response to a new Grammy category called best Asian pop music performance.

In July, BTS said it would not take part in the Grammys. The group had just had a huge year, including an album called ARIRANG that was number one on the Billboard 200 chart for three weeks. BTS said it was protesting awards "being divided by region or language."

The Recording Academy, which runs the Grammys, sees the new category differently. Its CEO, Harvey Mason Jr., said he was sad that BTS would not take part, but he respects the decision. He said artists who enter a category based on a style or place can still be considered in the general categories. He said the Asian pop category was created to celebrate the growth of pop music from Asia, and that more categories mean more artists get recognized.

After listening sessions with the Asian music community, the academy said on Thursday, Oct. 1, that it will go ahead with the category. Mason said, "We understand this conclusion will not satisfy everyone."

Stray Kids still have a big year. They topped the Billboard 200 twice in the past year, with the EP DO IT and the release THIS & THAT. Billboard has asked the group's representatives and the Grammys for comment.
why_it_matters: The story shows that musicians and award groups can disagree about how to honor music from different places and languages.
